title: Verify: buildSpriteSheet unit tests
summary: Unit tests for buildSpriteSheet width, height, frame count, layout and palette-only colours
description: Write TDD-style unit tests from REQ-S importing buildSpriteSheet, gridToRgba and PALETTE; pure functions need no mocks.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert 4 frames of 32x48 give 128x48, frameCount 4
Tests assert frame placement and unchanged pixels
Tests assert empty and mismatched input throw
Tests assert every sheet pixel colour is in the palette and bytes repeat identically
technical_constraints: Unit tests only; no browser or server
definition_of_done: Test file passes with the command given

steps.action: Import buildSpriteSheet from '../src/lib/spriteSheet' and gridToRgba from '../src/lib/gridToRgba'. Test 'size and count': four frames made by gridToRgba of a 48-row by 32-column grid filled with index i give width 128, height 48, frameWidth 32, frameHeight 48, frameCount 4. Test 'placement': read the pixel at x = i*32+5, y=10 for each i and assert it equals the RGB of PALETTE[i].
steps.code: expect(sheet).toMatchObject({ width: 128, height: 48, frameWidth: 32, frameHeight: 48, frameCount: 4 });
steps.command: cd game/frontend && npx vitest run tests/spriteSheet.test.ts

steps.action: Add tests: every pixel of the 4-frame sheet has RGB in the set of PALETTE colours; buildSpriteSheet([]) throws; frames of 2x2 and 3x2 throw; two calls give equal Array.from(data); the input frame data arrays are unchanged after the call.
steps.command: cd game/frontend && npx vitest run tests/spriteSheet.test.ts
steps.expected: Palette, error, determinism and non-mutation tests pass
